subject: RFI: IP outputs, warranty offsets and liability waterfall — Redwood response
messages:
From: Dana Miller <dana.miller@praxis-sys.com>
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@praxis-sys.com, evan.cho@praxis-sys.com
Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: RFI: Legal and IP questionnaire for Redwood Inference evaluation

Stephanie —

Thanks again for today’s overview. As part of our security and procurement review we have a short legal questionnaire focused on IP, indemnity, liability caps, and order-form terms. I’ve attached the questionnaire (Praxis_RFI_Legal_Questionnaire_v3.pdf) — can you return it completed and flag anything that would require a redline?

A few specific items we care most about up front:
- IP ownership for customer-specific fine-tuned models or prompt-tuned artifacts; do you assign or license?
- Liability cap: we typically request either a 12-month fee cap or $2M, whichever is higher — can you confirm your position and any exceptions?
- Open-source model carve-outs and export control obligations (we operate globally).
- Order form: billing cadence and refund/termination mechanics.

We’d appreciate a completed response by EOD Friday (5 business days). If you need more time, please propose a concrete timeline.

Thanks —
Dana Miller
Senior Procurement Lead
Praxis Systems
Praxis_RFI_Legal_Questionnaire_v3.pdf (attachment)

From: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: RFI: Legal and IP questionnaire for Redwood Inference evaluation

Hi Dana —

Appreciate the clear list — attaching our draft responses (Redwood_RFI_Response_IP_Indemnity.xlsx) and answering the top-line questions inline below so your team can triage quickly. I’ve looped in Karthik (contracts) and Ben (SE/account lead) to confirm technical and commercial bits.

Top-line answers (high level):
1) IP for customer-specific models/derivatives: Redwood does not assign underlying model or framework IP. We grant customers a perpetual, worldwide, non-exclusive, transferable license to customer-specific model outputs and to any customer-trained artifacts created exclusively from the customer’s data, subject to obligations in the order form. We call this out explicitly in section 2.2 of the attached response.

2) Liability cap: our standard is the greater of (a) 12 months of fees paid under the order form preceding the claim or (b) $1,000,000. We have carve-outs for gross negligence, willful misconduct, and breaches of data protection obligations. Karthik — please see note below for redline suggestion if Praxis requests higher threshold.

3) OSS carve-outs & export control: we include open-source model and third-party component carve-outs in our IP and indemnity language, and we comply with applicable export controls; we’ll include geographic-specific notes and an export-controls annex if required.

4) Order form mechanics: standard billing is monthly in arrears for hosted. We can offer quarterly prepaid billing for Dedicated/Private with committed capacity. Termination triggers and refund mechanics are in the order form annex — Ben, flag if Praxis needs a subscription/cancel walkthrough.

I’ve flagged five items in the attached spreadsheet that merit contract redlines or follow-up. If you prefer, we can convert those to a short tracked redline of your form.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Enterprise Sales Manager
Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 21 May 2026 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: RFI: Legal and IP questionnaire for Redwood Inference evaluation

Stephanie / Ben —

Reviewing Stephanie’s draft responses. I’ve attached a redline (Redwood_RFI_Response_IP_Indemnity_v2.docx) but calling out the main negotiation positions here so we’re aligned before returning to Praxis:

1) Liability cap: shift to greater of (i) 12 months of paid fees under the immediately preceding 12-month period or (ii) $1,000,000. If Praxis insists on a higher numeric cap (e.g., $2M), offer a graded escalation tied to committed spend (e.g., 1–3x the annualized committed fees for Dedicated contracts).

2) Carve-outs: preserve carve-outs for (a) willful misconduct and gross negligence, (b) IP indemnity where third-party claims are solely based on third-party-provided inputs, and (c) OSS/components where indemnity is limited to Redwood’s express modifications. Ensure export-control compliance clause references customer obligations to provide accurate export classifications.

3) IP assignment vs license: we will not assign core model IP or Redwood model weights. We can grant a perpetual, sublicensable license to customer-specific model artifacts derived solely from customer data and allow customers to deploy those artifacts in their environment (Private/Dedicated). For Hosted, include usage limits and retention/derivative handling in the order form.

4) Indemnity narrowing: narrow scope of customer indemnity to third-party claims arising from (i) customer-provided data, (ii) customer modifications, or (iii) breach of customer obligations (e.g., misuse, export violations). Redwood’s indemnity to customer should be focused on IP infringement for the services we provide and exclude open-source-only claims unless the claim arises from Redwood’s modifications.

5) Remedies & waterfall: include a liability waterfall that encourages remediation: cure first (patch/fix/replace), direct damages next (subject to cap), then injunctive relief for residual matters. We should offer to discuss a mutual SLA credit structure if Praxis is looking for operational remedies in lieu of higher monetary caps.

I’ll incorporate these into a tracked-redline version and we can send a clean response plus the redline as an optional negotiation artifact.

Karthik Iyer
Contracts Counsel (acting)
Redwood Inference

Stephanie / Karthik —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the redline — very helpful. A couple of follow-ups before we circulate internally:

1) Liability cap clarification: Praxis appreciates the greater-of approach but we need to better understand how "fees paid under the order form" will be calculated for hybrid deals (hosted + dedicated). Can you add an explicit calculation example in the order-form annex (monthly averaging, currency conversion rules, and treatment of prepaid credits)?

2) Data deletion and KMS: we need an explicit commitment on data deletion timelines after termination (standard for us is 90 days for hosted logs/temporary artifacts, 365 days for customer-supplied model artifacts unless otherwise negotiated), and confirmation that customer-managed keys (KMS) are supported for Private deployments. Can you add those bullets in the order form?

3) OSS carve-out example: please include a short illustrative example (e.g., where a claim arises solely from upstream OSS vulnerability unrelated to Redwood modifications) demonstrating limited Redwood exposure.

If you can add those items and provide the revised annex by EOD Monday, we’ll slot this into our procurement committee review on Tuesday.

Thanks —
Dana Miller
Senior Procurement Lead
Praxis Systems
